title: Problem Overview: Circle Covering
content: Erdős Problem #1121 asks: if circles C₁,...,Cₙ in ℝ² with radii r₁,...,rₙ have no separating line (no line disjoint from all circles that divides them into two non-empty groups), can they be covered by a single circle of radius Σrᵢ? Proved TRUE by Goodman and Goodman (1945). Generalizes to balls in ℝⁿ.
mathContext: The 'no separating line' condition captures when circles form a 'connected' cluster that cannot be split.

title: Circle and Line Structures
content: Circle: center (x,y) ∈ ℝ² and radius r > 0. Contains point p iff (p₁-x)² + (p₂-y)² ≤ r² (closed disk). Line: {(x,y) : ax + by = c} with (a,b) ≠ (0,0). A line is disjoint from a circle if it doesn't intersect the closed disk.

title: Separating Line and Connected Configuration
content: HasSeparatingLine: a line exists that is disjoint from all circles AND divides them into two non-empty groups (on opposite sides by signed distance). IsConnectedConfiguration: negation — no such separating line exists. Uses signedDistance(l, p) = (ax + by - c)/√(a²+b²) to determine which side of the line a point is on.
mathContext: This is the key condition of the theorem. Intuitively, circles that can't be separated are 'clustered together' in a way that allows covering.

title: Covering and Sum of Radii
content: Circle.covers C₁ C₂: every point in C₂ is also in C₁. Circle.coversAll C circles: C covers every circle in the set. sumOfRadii: Σᵢ rᵢ computed via Finset.sum. The theorem says the covering radius is EXACTLY the sum — this bound is tight.

title: ErdosConjecture1121 and Goodman-Goodman Theorem
content: ErdosConjecture1121: for any connected configuration of circles, there exists a covering circle of radius = sumOfRadii. goodman_goodman_theorem (axiom): this conjecture is TRUE. Proved in Amer. Math. Monthly (1945), 494-498, using convex hull arguments.

title: Special Cases: Two Circles and Overlapping
content: two_circles_case (axiom): two inseparable circles can be covered by a circle of radius r₁+r₂. CirclesOverlap: distance between centers ≤ r₁+r₂. overlap_implies_connected (axiom): if all pairs overlap, no separating line exists — overlapping is a sufficient condition for connected configuration.

title: Summary: SOLVED
content: erdos_1121_summary: ErdosConjecture1121 := goodman_goodman_theorem. The Erdős conjecture is TRUE. Connected circle configurations (no separating line) can be covered by a single circle of radius equal to the sum of all radii.
